Andrea James

Independent candidate for Governor & Lieutenant Governor, Massachusetts · Challenger

Community organizer and criminal justice advocate; founder and executive director of Families for Justice as Healing and the National Council for Incarcerated and Formerly Incarcerated Women and Girls

Andrea James is a Roxbury-born community organizer and former criminal defense attorney who founded two advocacy groups focused on incarcerated women and girls. She is a former Democrat who first filed to explore a Democratic run in 2025, then ran as an independent and gathered signatures to make the November ballot. She is on the November 3, 2026 ballot as an independent for governor, with Kayla Kittredge of Lowell as her running mate for lieutenant governor.

Where James stands

Immigration enforcement
Supports ending state cooperation with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Says the newly passed PROTECT Act does not go far enough to limit local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
Housing
Supports rent stabilization and building affordable housing. Advocates universal housing, including public housing for all.
Energy costs
Proposes lowering energy costs, including caps on utility costs and a path to publicly owned utilities.
Education
Supports equity in K-12 school funding, free public higher education and free childcare.
Government accountability
Has made Gov. Healey's ties to a 'dark money' nonprofit funded by corporations with business before the state a central issue of her campaign, and criticizes corporate funding of major campaigns.
Criminal justice / prisons
Opposes the plan to downsize and renovate MCI-Framingham and opposes building a new women's prison. Says she would grant clemency to as many women there as possible in her first week as governor so the prison can close.
Health care
Supports universal health care (Medicare for All with no copays or deductibles).
Cost of living / wages
Supports a $25 minimum wage and fare-free public transit.
Regional equity
Says state funding favors communities near Boston over western Massachusetts and pledges to address the gap.

Background

  • Born and raised in Boston (Roxbury); lifelong Massachusetts resident
  • B.A., University of Massachusetts Boston; J.D., Northeastern University School of Law
  • Founder and executive director, Families for Justice as Healing
  • Founder and executive director, National Council for Incarcerated and Formerly Incarcerated Women and Girls
  • Worked for state laws ending the shackling of incarcerated women during labor and allowing judges to consider primary-caretaker status at sentencing
  • Author, Upper Bunkies Unite (2013)
  • Former Democrat; running as an independent in 2026; endorsed by the Green-Rainbow Party (she is not its nominee)
